Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Clothes & getting dressed · Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

bead noun

also beads, string of beads

classical

Hor. S. 2.3.241 (Lewis & Short): a pearl
Verg. A. 1.655: monīle bācātum, a pearl necklace

bāca, bācae f.

noun, first declension

bead; anything round like a berry

(vōx dē margarītīs plērumque poētica: Hor., Ov.)

The berry word, in the series spelling, used of pearls and, in Prudentius, of the berry-shaped links of a chain (Lewis & Short); so the nearest classical word for a bead. Context tells it from a berry.

Examples

  • Bācās līnō īnserāmus.

    Let’s thread the beads on a string.composed

Other words

  • globulus, globulī m. — bead; literally a little ball

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. rosary, after Du Cange: sacrōrum globulōrum seriēs

    The bead of a rosary in later Latin; classically a little ball (Plin.). In the lexicon also the button.

  • sphaerula, sphaerulae f. — bead; a little ball

    noun, first declension · also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. rosary, after Erasmus: sphaerulae precātōriae; Vulg. Ex. 37.17 (Lewis & Short)

    Late Latin for a small ball; Erasmus’s word for the beads of a rosary.

See also necklace, pearl, marbles.

SourcesLewis & Short: baca · Lewis & Short: bacatus · Lewis & Short: globulus · Lewis & Short: sphaerula · Lewis & Short: linum

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. objects: rosary (beads). Traupman has only the pearl necklace, monīle baccātum (pp. 115, 117); Levi–Bini has no word.
